title: Credits Posted Outside the Statement Quarter: Effect on an Employer Benefit Charging Protest
content:
When an employer protests in writing the Employer Benefit Charging charges on a statement, disputing its base-period wages or its base-period status, credits already posted on the position can be taken out of the protest.

## Rule

Only credits posted on the position in a quarter other than the statement's quarter are looked at: where a credit for a recovered overpayment is among them, every credit posted on the position in a quarter other than the statement's quarter is taken out of the protest; where no recovered-overpayment credit is among them but credits for cancelled payments are, those cancelled-payment credits are taken out; otherwise nothing is taken out.

A credit's quarter is the calendar quarter in which the credit was posted, as shown on the credit entry. The statement's quarter is the quarter of the statement whose charges are protested.

## Decision table (credits posted outside the statement's quarter)

| A recovered-overpayment credit among them | Cancelled-payment credits among them | Taken out of the protest |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Either | Every credit posted outside the statement's quarter, of whatever reason |
| No | Yes | Only the cancelled-payment credits posted outside the statement's quarter |
| No | No | Nothing |

Credits posted inside the statement's quarter are never taken out and do not decide the row.

## Hypothetical cases (statement quarter: the third quarter)

| Credits on the position | Looked at | Taken out |
|---|---|---|
| Cancelled payment $80.00 (second quarter); relief $40.00 (fourth quarter); recovered overpayment $25.00 (third quarter) | $80.00 and $40.00 | $80.00 — no recovered-overpayment credit lies outside the third quarter |
| Recovered overpayment $30.00 (second quarter); cancelled payment $80.00 (second quarter); relief $40.00 (fourth quarter) | All three | $150.00 |
| Relief $40.00 (fourth quarter) only | $40.00 | Nothing |
